reason: The neural-induction environment is described as directing a stem-cell subset toward the neural lineage.
expectation: The signals will produce neural progenitors for later neuronal differentiation.

effect: The stem-cell subset became neural progenitors, which can produce neuronal and glial descendants.
reaction: The separate lineage branches make the next differentiation step clear.
reason: The neuronal differentiation signals are described as acting on neural progenitors.
expectation: The progenitors will develop into neuronal cells ready to acquire branches and axons.

effect: The progenitors differentiated into neuron cell bodies with buds for dendrites and axons.
reaction: The timeline clearly distinguishes progenitor division from neuronal differentiation.
reason: The dendrites' broad bases match the cell-body stubs and will add receiving branches.
expectation: The cell bodies will gain dendritic branches, ready for axons to be added.

alternatives.reason: The axons also match the cell bodies, so they might be added first.

effect: The cell bodies now have dendrites, leaving axons to complete the stated goal.
reaction: The bracket clarifies that the branches belong to the same cell.
reason: The axons have proximal ends that match the cell bodies and provide the conducting processes the goal calls for.
expectation: The neurons will gain axons and terminals alongside their receiving dendrites.

effect: The neurons now have dendrites and axons; the new goal is to connect and support them and examine a synaptic change.
reaction: The successive membrane-voltage panels help distinguish the signal from a packet travelling inside the axon.
reason: Excitatory synaptic contacts can connect the neurons and provide a starting point for examining their interactions.
expectation: The neurons will gain excitatory connections that transmit signals between them.

effect: The neurons now have excitatory connections, including converging inputs onto one receiving neuron.
reaction: The visible gaps make clear that the connected neurons remain separate cells.
reason: Inhibitory contacts complement the excitatory inputs and can show how combined signals affect firing.
expectation: The network will gain inhibitory inputs alongside its excitatory connections.

effect: The circuit now combines excitatory and inhibitory inputs, showing how inhibition can keep the receiving neuron below firing threshold.
reaction: The paired voltage traces make the effect of inhibition clear.
reason: Astrocytes support synapses by taking up potassium and released transmitter, matching the goal of supporting the circuit.
expectation: Astrocytes will be added around the circuit's synapses.

alternatives.reason: Myelin-forming cells could also provide support, potentially before astrocytes.

effect: Astrocytes are now interwoven with the neural circuits; the neurons and their synapses remain visible.
reaction: The support cells are added, though this result does not show their uptake role in detail.
reason: Oligodendrocytes form myelin sleeves around axons, providing another form of support for the circuit.
expectation: The circuit will gain myelin sleeves along its axons.

effect: The circuit is now central neural tissue with myelinated axon stretches and receptor-containing vesicles in a receiving dendrite.
reaction: The separate vesicle locations make the sending and receiving sides easier to distinguish.
reason: Repeated paired activity is the remaining item and is described at the highlighted connection, matching the goal of examining synaptic change.
expectation: The highlighted synapse will strengthen, possibly by adding receptors to the receiving membrane.

effect: The paired activity strengthened one existing synapse: equal transmitter input now produces a larger local response, while travelling impulses remain the same size. The chapter's goals are complete.
reaction: The before-and-after comparison usefully separates a stronger local response from a larger travelling impulse.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding inhibitory contacts was worthwhile because the planned paired voltage traces show how converging inputs can determine whether a neuron reaches firing threshold.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding astrocytes felt less informative: the result shows where they sit but does not illustrate the potassium and transmitter uptake described on the opening board.

surprise.text: The strengthened-synapse example distinguishes a larger local response from unchanged travelling impulse height, and shows the neighbouring connection remaining unchanged.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though adding dendrites and axons as separate pieces was a simplified assembly rather than an explanation of how those processes grow.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the neural circuit connects to other body systems; the comparisons of inhibition and synaptic strengthening made this chapter interesting.
